name: calm dark worn asphalt road with sparse aggregate, long hairline cracks, a repair patch and an oil stain, its unconnected edges crumbling into dirt with a darker broken lip and loose chunks, laid as a road network with crossroads and dead ends
label: wasteland_ruins/asphalt
reasons: 화풍: 칸 정보량이 기준보다 훨씬 낮음 (1/4)

surfaces.part: asphalt road tiles and dirt ground, flat terrain seen from above

answer.evidence: This is a terrain tileset sheet: dark asphalt road pieces (crossroads, T-junctions, dead ends, a corner, a single block and a large filled patch) laid on a brown dirt ground, all seen straight from above. The silhouette is a full 256-wide field on every row (0-191). No front face, eave, edge line or ellipse is drawn, and the road edges are crumbling lips, not vertical faces. It is a flat ground texture with no standing volume, so it reads as a top-down slab, which is expected for terrain.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate uses only 9 distinct colours in total and 4 visible tones per tile. That is above the grass reference (3) but well below the paving reference (7). The asphalt ramp is shallow, about 3 steps of slate blue-grey plus a darker lip, against the 5-6 steps Beodeul uses per material. Dirt has a few brown tones with speckle, so near-flat coverage is only 4%, but the texture is a repeated noise pattern and not shaded stone by stone. Edges carry a tinted dark lip (0% neutral), so the outline is not a black sticker line. Even so, the asphalt looks like a uniform mottled fill. The cracks, repair patch and oil stain are barely readable, and the patch has only a few dark marks. The road reads as thinner and flatter than the paving reference, so at this scale it falls short of the Beodeul bar.
